title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant
NN5, Northampton
15.00 per hour
37.5 hours per week
Temporary to Permanent
ASAP
About the Role
Are you an experienced Accounts Assistant looking for your next opportunity?
We are recruiting for an organised and proactive Accounts Assistant to join an established manufacturing business based in Northampton. This is a varied role offering the opportunity to support the day-to-day finance function.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous finance experience who enjoys working with numbers, takes pride in accuracy and is looking for a role with the potential to become permanent.

Key Responsibilities
- Supporting the day-to-day running of the finance department and maintaining accurate financial records.
- Processing purchase invoices and ensuring transactions are correctly coded and recorded.
- Managing supplier accounts, allocating payments and investigating statement discrepancies.
- Completing bank, credit card and balance sheet reconciliations.
- Processing expenses and maintaining petty cash records.
- Assisting with supplier payment runs and monitoring outstanding customer balances.
- Supporting credit control and following up on overdue payments.
- Assisting with VAT records, VAT returns and other financial reporting requirements.
- Preparing journals, accruals and prepayments where required.
- Supporting month-end procedures, management accounts and year-end preparation.
- Maintaining financial schedules and assisting with payroll-related reconciliations.
- Liaising with external accountants, suppliers and colleagues to resolve financial queries.
- Ensuring financial records are accurate, organised and maintained in line with company procedures.

About You
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant, Bookkeeper or similar finance role.
- Good understanding of purchase ledger, reconciliations and general bookkeeping.
- Familiarity with VAT and month-end accounting processes.
- Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills.
- Confident using Microsoft Excel and accounting software, ideally Xero or similar.
- Able to manage competing priorities and work to deadlines.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and a willingness to support the wider finance team.

Interested? If you have finance experience and are looking for your next opportunity, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today to find out more, or please send your CV to (url removed)

title: Administrator
description:
Administrator (Minute taking)

Location: Kettering, NN16 0 SW or Northampton NN1 1 ED (work can be done remotely once trained)

Working Hours: 22 hours per week, 3 days per week with flexibility on start and finish times (either 8am-4pm, 8.30am-4.30pm or 9am-5pm)

Length: 3 months initially

Start Date: ASAP

This is a fantastic opportunity for a highly organised, detail-focused individual with strong listening and written skills to contribute to safeguarding processes in a flexible, mostly remote role.

About the role

You will play a key role in producing accurate, high-quality minutes from recordings of statutory meetings such as Child Protection Conferences and reviews.

With no requirement to travel between sites, your focus will be on efficiently listening to recordings and producing structured minutes using set templates.

The role requires emotional resilience, as the content discussed within meetings can be sensitive in nature.

Key responsibilities
- Listen to recorded statutory meetings
- Produce clear, accurate, and timely minutes using set templates
- Record key decisions, actions, and outcomes in line with safeguarding protocols
- Ensure documentation is completed to a high standard and submitted within deadlines
- Upload and manage records within internal systems (Liquidlogic)
- Work collaboratively with the wider minute-taking team and attend regular virtual catch-ups
- Maintain confidentiality and professionalism at all times

What we're looking for

Strong minute-taking or transcription experience

Excellent listening skills and attention to detail

Ability to produce clear, well-structured written documents

Comfortable working independently in a remote environment

Competent IT skills

Ability to manage workload and meet deadlines

Emotional resilience when dealing with sensitive subject matter

Experience within Children's Services or safeguarding environments (desirable)

Working arrangements & benefits

2-day onsite induction, with equipment provided for remote working

Weekly virtual team check-ins

Monthly team meeting (at One Angel Square, Northampton or William Knibb Meeting Suite, Kettering)

Flexible working days (3 days per week)

title: Attendance Administrator
description:
Attendance Administrator

Location: Northampton, Northamptonshire
Salary (Apply online only) a day
Contract: Full Time, Temp to Perm
Hours: 8am to 4pm

Attendance Administrator

Are you organised, proactive and passionate about supporting young people to achieve their full potential? We are seeking a reliable and enthusiastic Attendance Administrator to join our busy secondary school office team.

The successful candidate will play a key role in monitoring and promoting student attendance, maintaining accurate records and working closely with students, parents/carers, teaching staff and the wider pastoral team to improve attendance and punctuality across the school.

Key Responsibilities
- Monitor and record daily student attendance, ensuring registers are completed accurately and promptly.
- Follow up on student absences, contacting parents/carers by telephone, email or text to establish reasons for absence.
- Maintain accurate attendance records and update the school's management information system.
- Ideally, use Arbor to record attendance, update student information and generate attendance reports.
- Identify patterns of absence and lateness, bringing concerns to the attention of the appropriate staff.
- Support the school in implementing attendance procedures and improving overall attendance rates.
- Assist with preparing attendance reports, letters and documentation for meetings.
- Work collaboratively with pastoral leaders, Heads of Year, the safeguarding team and the Senior Leadership Team.
- Maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information in accordance with school policies and data protection requirements.
- Provide general administrative support to the school office when required.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for someone who:
- Has excellent organisational skills and a strong attention to detail.
- Has good written and verbal communication skills.
- Is confident using IT systems, including Microsoft Word, Excel and email.
- Has basic knowledge of Arbor or experience using a school management information system (desirable).
- Can communicate professionally and sensitively with parents/carers and students.
- Is proactive in following up absences and resolving attendance queries.
- Can work independently, prioritise tasks and meet deadlines in a busy school environment.
- Understands the importance of confidentiality, safeguarding and accurate record-keeping.
- Has previous administrative experience, ideally within a school or educational setting (desirable).

What We Offer
- The opportunity to make a positive difference to students' education and wellbeing.
- A supportive and welcoming team environment.
- Opportunities to develop your administrative skills and knowledge of school attendance systems.
- Training and support to develop your understanding of Arbor and school attendance procedures, where required.

How to Apply

If you are an organised, approachable and motivated individual who would like to contribute to improving student attendance and achievement, we would love to hear from you.

title: Business Development Executive
description:
Business Development Executive/Researcher - Commercial Fit-Out & Workspace Solutions

Location: Northampton (Office-Based)
Salary: 28,000 - 40,000 (DOE) + Performance related bonus (OTE 10k, uncapped)

Hours: Monday to Friday 07:30am - 4:30pm (Flexibility as required)

Holidays: 22 days + additional 1 day birthday leave + statutory

Are you naturally curious, commercially minded, and skilled at uncovering opportunities others miss? Do you enjoy researching businesses, building relationships, and playing a key role in driving growth without the pressure of a traditional hard-sales environment?

If this sounds like you, a leading specialist in commercial warehouse and industrial fit-out solutions is looking for a Business Development Executive / Researcher to join their growing team.

About the Company

This ambitious and fast-growing business delivers turnkey warehouse, logistics and office fit-out projects across the UK. Working with organisations in the logistics, warehousing and manufacturing sectors, they help businesses transform and scale their operational spaces quickly and efficiently. With significant growth plans and increasing demand for their services, they are investing heavily in their business development capabilities to support the next stage of expansion.

What's the Role About?

This is not your typical business development position.

You'll focus on identifying future opportunities before projects are actively being tendered, using a combination of research, prospecting and relationship-building activities to create a strong pipeline for the commercial team.

You'll:
- Research and identify businesses that fit the ideal customer profile.
- Build relationships with senior decision-makers across target organisations.
- Generate qualified opportunities and meetings for the sales team.
- Gather valuable market intelligence and commercial insight.
- Position the business as the preferred partner when future projects arise.

Key Responsibilities
- Research and qualify prospective customers across logistics, warehousing, manufacturing and industrial sectors.
- Use CRM platforms, LinkedIn and prospecting tools to identify key contacts and opportunities.
- Conduct outbound phone, email and LinkedIn outreach to directors, owners and senior decision-makers.
- Generate Marketing Qualified Leads (MQLs) and support the progression of opportunities through the sales funnel.
- Build detailed account profiles including ownership structures, growth plans and operational requirements.
- Nurture long-term relationships with prospects and referral partners.
- Maintain accurate CRM records, activity reporting and pipeline updates.
- Identify early buying signals and future project opportunities ahead of competitors.

Requirements

About You

We're looking for someone who is:
- Confident communicating with senior stakeholders and business leaders.
- Naturally inquisitive with strong research and investigative skills.
- Organised, detail-oriented and comfortable managing multiple opportunities.
- Resilient and professional when conducting outbound outreach.
- Relationship-focused and commercially aware.
- Motivated by targets, growth and delivering measurable outcomes.

Experience in business development, lead generation, appointment setting, account management or sales support would be advantageous, although attitude, curiosity and drive are equally important. Experience using LinkedIn Sales Navigator, CRM systems or prospecting tools would also be beneficial.

Benefits

What's in it for you?
- Join a growing business with ambitious expansion plans.
- Clear progression opportunities into Business Development, Sales or Account Management.
- Work closely with senior leadership and gain valuable commercial exposure.
- Competitive salary with performance-related bonus potential.
- Supportive, collaborative and entrepreneurial team environment.
- Opportunity to develop highly transferable sales, research and relationship-management skills.

If you're looking for a role where your research skills, commercial awareness and relationship-building ability can make a direct impact on business growth, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today or get in touch for a confidential conversation about this exciting opportunity.

title: Credit Controller
salary_text: £28000 - £32000 per year (hybrid working and flex hours)
description:
As a Credit Controller in the business services industry, based in Northampton, you'll play a key role in managing and maintaining the company's credit and collections processes. Your day-to-day will involve ensuring timely payments, resolving account queries, and supporting the smooth running of the accounting and finance department.

Client Details

A company in the business services industry located in Northampton.

Description

Manage and recover outstanding debt relating to fees across multiple locations.

Review and prioritise aged debt ledgers, focusing on high-value and long-outstanding accounts.

Contact responsible parties by telephone, email and letter to secure payment of overdue balances.

Investigate and resolve account queries, disputed charges and billing discrepancies that may delay payment.

Negotiate payment arrangements and repayment plans in line with company policies.

Monitor agreed payment schedules and follow up on broken arrangements.

Liaise closely with Regional Managers and Finance teams to obtain information required to support debt recovery activities.

Maintain accurate records of all communications, payment commitments and collection activity.

Escalate high-risk or non-responsive accounts through the appropriate internal and legal recovery processes.

Reconcile customer accounts and allocate payments accurately.

Profile

A successful Credit Controller should have:
- Previous experience in credit control or a similar role within accounting and finance.
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational abilities.
- Confident communication skills to liaise with clients and internal teams.
- Proficiency in relevant accounting software and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- The ability to work efficiently under pressure and meet deadlines.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and resolving account issues.

Job Offer
- Competitive salary of up to 32,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Permanent position based in Northampton.
- Opportunity to work in the business services industry.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

description:
Could you work in Internal Sales driving sales growth in a brilliant Manufacturing business Are you confident in working with external customers and internal teams in an internal engineering sales or internal technical sales role Are you well organised and proactive in progressing customer requirements from initial costing through manufacturing and to dispatch

Kingscroft has been asked to recruit for an Internal Sales candidate for a fast paced manufacturing business. As the ideal candidate you will have had experience of working in a Customer Account Management or an Internal Sales Exec role in a manufacturing , technical or engineering setting. You will be confident of acting as the focal point for customer orders; liaising closely with external sales teams initially and then through engineering, manufacturing, quality and dispatch.

Customer Service Communication
- Act as the primary point of contact for day-to-day customer queries, requests, and issues.
- Respond to telephone, email, and online enquiries promptly and professionally.
- Provide customers with product information, pricing, lead times, and order updates.

Sales Support

- Support external sales representatives with account management and follow-ups.
- Identify upselling or cross-selling opportunities where appropriate.

Order Processing Administration
- Process sales orders accurately, ensuring all details are correct and captured in the system.
- Liaise with production, purchasing, logistics, and finance teams to ensure timely fulfilment of customer orders.
- Maintain customer records and update CRM or ERP systems.
- Monitor stock levels and communicate availability or delays to customers.

Problem Resolution

- Investigate and resolve delivery, product, or invoice discrepancies.

This is a fantastic opportunity to take on a key role for a business that is looking strengthen its internal sales and account management processes to enable continued growth and expansion. Your sales, costing and proactive skill set will vital for your success in this post.

Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record
